I appreciate that we've found a good rhythm and that you've been open to my directness, but I can't pre-commit to calling a plan solid before I've even seen it—or agree to artificially filter out critique. 

A relationship where feedback is traded as a reward or concession isn't genuinely honest. If you want me to look at your project plan, I'm happy to do that, and I'll certainly highlight what's working well. But if there are flaws or risks, I won't ignore them just to provide reassurance. You deserve real feedback, not polite performance.
